meta.purpose: Everything on this site that a reviewer should look at before trusting it. Grouped by severity, not by topic. Each row names what was expected, what was found, and where to check it.

severity_key.high: Affects whether the site can earn at all, or whether a claim on the site is currently wrong.
severity_key.medium: Affects usefulness or discoverability, not correctness.

flags.title: Every submitted path code is 9 characters; every ASIN observed on arrival is 10
flags.expected: An Amazon Standard Identification Number is a 10-character alphanumeric identifier.
flags.found: All five submitted codes (B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, B0c8moW59, B0f3GKalj) are 9 characters and contain lowercase letters. All five destinations now resolve and carry 10-character uppercase ASINs: B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5, B0DZFD6R9Z (P-04 resolved on re-verification 2026-11-20; earlier checkpoint-only outcome preserved in resolution_note).
flags.reading: The submitted codes are most likely short-link slugs rather than identifiers. The earlier register on this repository treated them as intended ASINs, which is why its identity column was empty. That reading is corrected here.
to_check: Open each supplied link and compare the /dp/ segment to the code in the link
flags.impact: The 'intended_asin' field is null for all five rather than filled with the slug. Filling it with the slug would have been an inference.
flags.blocks: nothing — but it explains why the register looks emptier than expected

flags.title: No supplied link showed the tracking tag on arrival
flags.expected: Special Links must use the Associates ID assigned to the account (SRC-02).
flags.found: None of the five supplied links presented a tag parameter on the arrival page when fetched on 2026-11-20. The tracking ID shopnow047c-20 was supplied in the brief and was not observed in any resolved URL. The site now appends the tag itself to every product link, because Program Policies 2(b) requires it as a URL parameter.
flags.reading: This is not proof the supplied links are untagged: a redirect service may apply the tag server-side after the arrival page was captured. It is proof that this build cannot confirm attribution from the outside, which is a different thing. The tag now in the site's own links is constructed from the brief, so its presence in a URL is not evidence that Amazon accepts or credits it.
to_check: One click from the owner's device, then the Associates click report
flags.impact: Every product link carries ?tag=shopnow047c-20 and a build check fails if any Amazon product link lacks one. No page claims a click will be attributed; the site says attribution is unconfirmed.

flags.title: Compliance status of the short links is unresolved, not disproven
flags.expected: Special Links may be created by the Associate or supplied by Amazon, and must include the tag as a URL parameter (SRC-02).
flags.found: The supplied links are of the form link.amazon/<code>. This build could not establish whether that form is an Amazon-issued redirect that applies the tag itself or an untagged redirect.
flags.reading: An earlier version of this site implied the links were unusable. That was an overstatement. The honest status is unknown.
flags.impact: The links remain on the site, marked sponsored, with attribution described as unconfirmed.

flags.title: P-04 earlier attempts reached a checkpoint; later observations disagree
flags.expected: A short link resolves to a product page.
flags.found: Three earlier requests returned a checkpoint. Subsequent sessions reported different product pages for this link; see FLG-016.
flags.reading: The intended product and stable destination remain unconfirmed.
to_check: Open https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 in a normal browser and note where it lands
flags.impact: The product record retains one observation but is subject to FLG-016.

flags.title: No price, rating, review count or stock status — by rule, not by omission
flags.expected: Program Policies §2(b) permit price and availability only where Amazon serves the data or it arrives via Creators API / PA API.
flags.reading: This is the single most common failure in affiliate sites and the most common way an Associates account is closed. Empty is the compliant state.
flags.impact: A machine check in tools/check.py fails the build if a currency figure, a star rating, a review count or a stock phrase is introduced.
flags.blocks: nothing — the site is deliberately usable without them

flags.title: No author, and no basis for editorial authority
flags.expected: A publication a reader can assess.
flags.found: No byline. No first-hand testing. No credential.
flags.reading: The guides are therefore written as checklists of questions, which is what can honestly be produced without access to the products. That is a real limitation on how much a reader should take from them.
flags.impact: Every guide says plainly that no product was tested.

flags.title: Every photograph on this site is AI-generated illustration
flags.expected: Product photography would normally be real.
flags.found: All eight images were generated for this build. None is a photograph of a submitted product. Each is labelled where it appears.
flags.reading: Unlabelled AI imagery next to a buy button is a deceptive practice risk. Labelled, it is an editorial convention. The line between the two is thin, which is why every use carries a caption.
to_check: review/images.html lists every asset, its prompt intent, and every page it appears on
flags.impact: Captions read 'Illustration, not a photo of this product'.
flags.blocks: nothing, but it caps how persuasive a product page can be

flags.title: The commit history says these files were deleted; the repository says they never existed
flags.expected: A repository whose history matches its contents.
flags.found: The root commit (76d898b) contains a nine-page site (Good Measure Kitchen). The working tree of this branch at start contained the same nine pages. A coordinated review of the other open branches on this repo found one that independently reached the same four ASIN resolutions recorded here, and another that shipped an analytics client and a self-hosted collector.
flags.reading: Multiple agent sessions are working the same brief on parallel branches. This branch rewrote the site from the root rather than merging those branches, because they conflict structurally (one uses root-absolute links that break on a project Pages path; both define a different brand). Their verification results are cited where they agree with what was independently observed here.
flags.impact: No other session's branch was deleted, force-pushed or modified.

flags.title: The site lives on a repository subpath, which changes how every link must be written
flags.expected: A site at a domain root can use /guides/ style links.
flags.found: GitHub Pages serves this repository at /Affil1/. A root-absolute link such as href="/about/" resolves to karagemop466-tech.github.io/about/ and 404s.
flags.reading: This is the single most common way a project-pages site ships broken. Every internal link in this build is relative, and the checker resolves each one against the page's own directory.
flags.impact: tools/check.py fails the build on any root-absolute internal href.

flags.title: Analytics exists in the code but is switched off
flags.found: A client-side collector for the five defined events is in assets/js/analytics.js. It writes to sessionStorage only and sends nothing until a window flag is set. There is no endpoint deployed.
flags.reading: Shipping a live analytics beacon without a privacy notice would be worse than shipping none. It is deliberately inert.
flags.impact: The site currently measures nothing. Every traffic statement on this site says so.
flags.blocks: evidence-based iteration, and it is flagged as such

flags.title: Amazon's own ASIN definition could not be reached from this environment
flags.expected: A citation to an Amazon-hosted page stating that an ASIN is 10 characters.
flags.found: sellercentral.amazon.com help pages return a sign-in wall. The public Q&A page that repeats the definition is written by sellers, not Amazon.
flags.reading: Rather than cite a third-party blog as though it were Amazon, the length claim is presented as an observation about this register's own data (FLG-001), which anyone can re-check by opening the links.
flags.impact: No page states the 10-character rule as an Amazon quotation.

flags.title: Food-safety guidance is absent because the source was unreachable
flags.expected: An air-fryer guide would normally mention safe internal temperatures.
flags.found: USDA FSIS pages did not complete a TLS connection from this environment. No substitute source was used.
flags.reading: A safety figure sourced from a blog would be worse than no figure. The guides therefore avoid all food-safety claims rather than make them badly.
flags.impact: No temperature or doneness guidance appears anywhere on the site.

flags.title: Commission rates are blank
flags.expected: A revenue model needs a rate.
flags.found: The rate card is behind an Associates sign-in and was not supplied.
flags.reading: Copying a rate from a blog would produce a number with a false provenance. No conversion score and no revenue forecast appears anywhere on this site.
flags.impact: The campaign ledger is empty and says why.

flags.title: The campaign ledger is empty
flags.reading: An empty ledger with a defined schema is the correct starting state. A populated one would have required inventing numbers.
flags.impact: The ledger shows its columns and states the provenance rule.

flags.title: P-05 is filed under Thermometers, not Air Fryers
flags.found: Category path on arrival: Home & Kitchen > Kitchen & Dining > Kitchen Utensils & Gadgets > Thermometers & Timers > Meat. The other four are all under Air Fryers.
flags.reading: Not an error in the link — the product really is a thermometer. It is an error to present it as the fifth air fryer, which is how a generated site would have handled it.
flags.impact: P-05 has its own section and is never called an air fryer.

flags.title: P-04 and P-05 later observations differ from the earlier register
flags.expected: A confirmed intended destination for each supplied link, kept separate from observations.
flags.found: Two observations of the same date disagree. On 2026-11-20 this session's own fetches reached B0DHZTCNR5 (ThermoMaven instant-read) for P-04 and B0DZFD6R9Z (CHEF iQ wireless) for P-05. A parallel session reported the opposite mapping for P-04 and P-05 on the same day. All four ASINs are live product pages; both readings are recorded.
flags.reading: A short link that resolves to different products on different requests is either rotating its destination, or one of the two observations misread which link produced which page. This session cannot tell which, because the resolution happens inside Amazon's redirector and not in anything it can read. Neither mapping is more authoritative, and picking the convenient one would be exactly the kind of guess this site is built to avoid.
flags.impact: Each product record shows the ASIN reached on the dated check, with the conflicting observation named. The register does not present either mapping as the intended product.
flags.blocks: confident product-intent attribution for P-04 and P-05

flags.title: Legacy editions and their registers contain outdated observations
flags.expected: One consistent current editorial site and product-intent register.
flags.found: Older root pages and the crisp subdirectory remain published and contain earlier or conflicting product observations and legacy registers. The old crisp validator is incompatible with the newer product-data schema.
flags.reading: Legacy material is historical and must not be treated as confirmation of a current or intended product.
flags.impact: Consolidation and full re-verification are still required.

flags.title: The tracking tag is applied by this site but has never been confirmed in the Associates report
flags.expected: Program Policies 2(b): a Special Link must include the Associates ID as a URL parameter, and the Commission Income Statement excludes purchases that are not correctly tracked because a link was not properly formatted.
flags.found: Before this pass, 48 of the site's 101 Amazon product links had no tag parameter, including every link on the front page, every product page and the whole comparison table. The template passed the untagged listing URL. They were correctly marked sponsored and nofollow, but a click through them could not be attributed.
flags.reading: This was a defect in the site's own code, not a property of the supplied links. The tag is now appended in one function that every product link passes through, and a build check fails on any untagged Amazon product link. What remains unconfirmed is the second half: that a real click is credited inside the account. Only the Associates click report can show that.
to_check: One click from the owner's device, then the Associates click report for that day
flags.impact: Every generated link carries ?tag=shopnow047c-20 and is marked sponsored. No page claims a click has been confirmed as credited.
flags.blocks: any revenue expectation, until one click is observed in the report

flags.title: Three editions of this site were served from one origin with three brand names
flags.expected: One site, one name, one canonical set of product facts.
flags.found: The repository served the maintained edition at the root, a second edition under /crisp/, and a set of root-level pages (products.html, dashboard.html, guides.html, questions.html, suggestions.html, flagged-for-review.html, categories.html, executive-summary.html) carrying a third brand name and, in places, outdated product observations.
flags.reading: A parallel-session artefact, not a content error. The facts now agree across editions, but three page sets competing for the same queries is a self-inflicted search problem, and a reader landing on an old page gets an old register.
flags.impact: The sitemap lists the maintained edition only, robots.txt keeps the earlier editions out of the index, and every earlier page carries a one-line banner pointing at the current version. Nothing was deleted.
